newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold may crawl higher but upside capped.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold may crawl higher but upside capped.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold may creep higher after it closed above $340 on Thursday but gains will be capped at $342.50 and the overall downside bias remains intact, analysts said.
Silver was trading in a range with the upside seen limited at $4.80/$4.85 for now.
Platinum had good support at $370.00.

GOLD - Bullion may struggle higher on Friday with short covering after a firmer Thursday close but it is unlikely to overcome the solid resistance at $342.50 which held stubbornly in rallies last week, dealers said.
It was also unlikely to react to the landslide victory for the Labour Party in the UK general election on Thursday.

"It's an order-driven market. In Europe we don't have the speculators any more. There is physical offtake, which brings underlying support, and funds are chart-driven," said Felder Rene, precious metals dealer at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS).

The market awaits key U.S. payrolls data expected out at 1230 GMT. Any inflationary pressures could put a positive spin on gold, but gains were likely to be capped by fears over the prospect of future central bank sales, dealers said.
"All advances are stopped by this feeling that once prices go higher you have the producers and you have the central banks," said Rene.
While bullion held below $345.00, the risk of a slide to test the February 12 low of $336.15 remained intact, analysts said.
"Support above $340 continues to hold, though with a potential bearish wedge pattern developing, a downside break remains the favoured direction," said Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
By 0800 GMT spot bullion was quoted at $340.10/$340.40 an ounce, barely changed from Thursday's late close of $340.20/$340.70.
SILVER - A strong close on Thursday gave a technical face lift to silver, but many analysts still believed upward prospects were limited to $4.80-$4.85 in the near term.

Rene of UBS said major players were short of the market and any further gains could spark a covering bout. The metal was also supported by the liquidity squeeze in platinum and palladium, although these were stuck in a range.
But he reckoned $4.60 was a critical support level for silver.
"If it breaks we have another 40 cents to go," Rene said.
Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said a crossing of the nearby moving averages confirmed the positive trend in silver.
"Look up for further challenges of overhead resistance," he said.
By 0815 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.74/$4.76 an ounce, unchanged from Thursday's finish in New York.
PLATINUM - The market may glean support from palladium if tightness, due to protracted delays in Russian supplies, resumes.
Support was pegged strongly at $370.00, while resistance was around $375.00-$380.00, analysts said.
By 0815 GMT spot platinum was indicated at $372.50/$373.50, down from New York's close of $373.60/$374.60.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
